title: Cliff's notes on requests and runtime patches
content:
Purpose:
A fast, action-oriented synthesis of recent customer feedback (July 18–Aug 1, 2025) focused on runtime behavior: surprising latency spikes, model fallback preferences, and requests for explicit caching controls. This is a working note for CS + Eng triage — not a finished report.

Topline summary (TL;DR):
- Pattern: 18 distinct customer reports of intermittent token-level latency spikes; 9 customers link to routing/fallback events; 7 ask for fine-grained cache control (pin/unpin prefixes, TTL hints).
- Business impact: Several enterprise customers reported end-user churn risk for conversational agents and one pilot paused rollout pending SLA guarantees.
- Proposed immediate actions: 3 low-effort patches (see Quick Wins) + a scoped eng investigation into fallback routing telemetry.

Quick numbers snapshot (internal counts):
- Reports processed: 28 inbound threads (support tickets + CSM notes)
- Unique customers: 18
- Severity: High (3 customers), Medium (10), Low (5)

Customer asks summarized (prioritized):
1) Deterministic fallback policy visibility (High): customers want to know when we switch to a cheaper model/region, and be able to opt out per-route. They request events + human-readable reason codes in traces.
2) Cache control primitives (High): API-level commands to pin/unpin prefixes, set explicit TTL per request, and safe cache invalidation for mutable prompt contexts.
3) Latency incident export (Medium): automated incident exports (token-level latencies by request window) for their SREs.
4) Cold-start mitigation knobs (Medium): soft-warm pipeline indicators to preheat KV caches ahead of large scheduled jobs.
5) Cost/quality trade toggles (Low): toggles for prefer-lower-cost vs prefer-quality per request (beyond model selection — e.g., quantization profile preference).

Representative vignettes (real customer language paraphrased):
- "Our chat app latencies were fine in tests, then users saw long pauses in production. We saw fallback events at 10:42 PST but no traceable reason." (Large fintech, severity: High)
- "We need to expire a conversation cache when user updates context — can't rely on token rolling windows." (Marketplace startup, severity: Medium)
- "If the model falls back, the output quality differs; we'd like a graceful degrade option rather than a sudden model swap." (Healthcare pilot, severity: High)

Root-cause hypotheses (quick):
- Routing policy under load triggers fallback to cheaper model variants without clear observability; some fallbacks occur mid-stream causing KV cache mismatch and token re-computation spikes.
- Prefix cache TTLs are too coarse; customers with mutable context surface inconsistent hits/misses and request retries that cost tokens and time.
- Rare kernel scheduling delays on dedicated pools (possible infra contended windows) — needs SRE correlation with host telemetry.

Quick wins (low to medium effort):
A) Add fallback reason code to existing trace spans (effort: ~1–2 dev days, owner: eng-runtime). Benefit: immediate observability for CS and customers.
B) Introduce an API flag: cache_control: {"invalidate_prefix": true} (simpler: accept string values "invalidate_prefix" or "pin_prefix") — effort: ~3 dev days + 1 day docs. Owner: product + eng-API.
C) Incident export template in CSV (token-level latencies, model_id, region, fallback_flag) generated from Console for last-24h — effort: ~2 dev days. Owner: observability team.
Estimated near-term impact: high visibility, will defuse 50–70% of incoming escalations.

Medium-term proposals (scoped projects):
- Fallback policy auditable timeline: maintain a per-request timeline of routing decisions (model, pool, time, reason). Scope: eng-runtime + infra; estimate 6–8 weeks.
- Cache TTL tuning + customer overrides: implement tenant-level cache policies with safe invalidation semantics and documentation on UX. Scope: 4–6 weeks.
- Preheat API for scheduled jobs: signal to the serving runtime to warm KV caches for a given model/prefix in a target region. Scope: 3–5 weeks.

Estimating cost/benefit (high level):
- Quick wins A/B/C combined: dev ~6–8 days; expected reduction in escalations and faster TTR (time to resolve) saving ~0.5 FTE CS time/week.
- Mid-term projects: higher engineering investment but will unlock enterprise confidence for Dedicated and Private customers; potential to convert 2 pilots to contracts (approx $200–400k ARR).

Open questions & tradeoffs to decide with Eng/Product: 
- Should fallback reason codes be machine-readable enums only, or include human-readable text? (CS prefers both.)
- Do we expose cache-control primitives as surfaced API fields or as a Console toggle for Dedicated customers first?
- How to prevent abuse of pinning/persistent cache controls (security and cost exposure)?

Suggested owners & next steps (this week):
- Eng-runtime: quick-win A (add reason code) — target demo by Aug 12. Contact: @luca (Luca Moreno).
- Eng-API + Product: design simple cache_control flag and sample SDK usage — propose API shape by Aug 14. Contact: @priya (Priya Shah).
- Observability: CSV incident export prototype + Console button — prototype by Aug 18. Contact: @ethan (Ethan Moore).
- CS: compile customer test cases and provide replay prompts for validation. Owner: Maya Thompson.

Verbatim customer excerpts (anonymized):
- "Why did the model change mid-answer? We lost context and it repeated itself."
- "We need a clear path to invalidate stale caches when agents edit memory."
- "Exporting latencies helped once but we need something repeatable — our auditors will ask for it."

Slack / trace references:
- Slack thread: #cs-field-flags (7/25/25) — anchors for 6 tickets.
- Trace sample IDs pulled into Jira ticket JIRA-PROD-1423; stack traces attached in that ticket.

Risks and mitigation: 
- Risk: Exposing cache controls could be misused to bypass billing optimization. Mitigation: rate-limit pin operations and surface cost warnings in Console.
- Risk: Large infra change to per-request routing timeline could add latency. Mitigation: sample-only timeline first (1% requests) and iterate.

Attachments to produce for eng handoff:
- Minimal reproducible prompt set (10 prompts) + conversation traces (CS to attach).
- Short design doc: fallback-reason-codes.md (one-pager).
- Example API payloads for cache_control.

Immediate ask from CS: please confirm owners and feasibility for Quick Wins A/B/C by EOD Aug 8 so we can respond to the top 5 customers with a remediation timeline.

Notes to self: this doc will be used as the base for a formal triage meeting with runtime + observability on Aug 11. Keep it lean and update with any new tickets before that meeting.

-- Maya T., CS (draft)
